text:
irene: heads-up while onboarding magnet-30b-v2 (int4) on multi-GPU: we see context "drops" when the generation crosses a shard boundary at ~16,384 tokens. model starts to forget entities from earlier in the doc; float16 baseline doesn't show this.

sam: can you be more specific by "drop"? are tokens missing from output or logits suddenly bias?

irene: tokens re-reference older names incorrectly and sometimes repeat a recent noun as if earlier history evaporated. not blanking, more like a short-term memory swap.

prateek: suspicious. this smells like a KV memcpy / shard-index misalignment at wrap. are you using `kv_shard_stride=16384` default?

irene: yes default stride. run flags: `--model magnet-30b-v2 --quant=int4 --max-tokens=20000 --kv_shard_stride=16384 --shard_swap=true` and `KVCACHE_DEBUG=1`

alon: any KVCACHE_DEBUG excerpt around the boundary? also check whether `kv_index` transitions from rel->abs correctly when crossing GPU shards.

irene: pasted excerpt:
```
[16380] kv: writing shard0 idx=16379 -> host_offset=0x7f8a2ffc
[16384] kv: rotate-shard boundary triggered, target_shard=1
[16385] kv: rel_idx=16384 -> abs_idx=16384
[16386] rotary_phase: 0.2345 -> 0.2346
[16387] out_token: "Margaret" -> "Margaret" -> OK
[16392] out_token: "said" -> "said" -> OK
[16395] out_token: "later" -> "Margaret" (incorrect)
```

maya: that log shows successful handoff but corrupt association later. Could be a memory aliasing bug on memcpy between shards or inconsistent per-layer quant params when loading shard partials.

prateek: try forcing `--kv_shard_stride=8192` (smaller boundary) and `--no_shard_swap` to see whether the issue follows the boundary or the swap codepath. also run an int8 baseline.

irene: queued three quick runs: (A) stride=8192 + shard_swap=true (B) shard_swap=false (C) quant_fallback=int8. ci job 4899998889 queued.

ci-bot: nightly_pipeline/run/4899998889 - magnet-30b-v2-shard-bisect queued. artifacts -> s3://redwood-ci/runs/4899998889/

sam: if (B) fixes, we likely have a race in the swap logic. if (A) still fails at new boundary, it points at copy/align assumptions. gather GPU memcpy logs and check `cudaMemcpyAsync` offsets.

alon: small gotcha: int4 packed tensors can have byte-alignment differences across shards; if pack/unpack routines assume 128-byte alignment but runtime gives different offsets, you get shifted values causing downstream attention mis-indexing. add assert that unpacked KV hash matches pre-swap checksums.

irene: preliminary results: (A) failure moved to ~8192 boundary (same symptom). (B) shard_swap=false stable to 20k. (C) int8 stable. looks like swap code + int4 packing alignment.

prateek: great repro. next steps: 1) add a swap-time checksum/CRC on packed KV blobs and validate on the target shard after memcpy; 2) run microbench that intentionally misaligns the pack alignment to reproduce corruption; 3) add unit to unpack/repacks roundtrip test for int4 packing with different offsets.

sam: also add a short circuit in swap code: if CRC mismatch, fallback to copying via a verified CPU unpack-repack path (slower but correct) and emit a SLI event for visibility.

irene: opening ML ticket ML-9998 with sample outputs, packed blob hex dumps and KVCACHE_DEBUG. attached failing tail: "...and then Margaret later Margaret said" (shows the swap-induced name repeat).

ci-bot: nightly_pipeline/run/4899998890 - artifact upload complete. s3://redwood-ci/runs/4899998889/

maya: thanks for the clear repro. prateek, want me to take the CRC fallback and a small synthetic test while you dig into the pack/unpack logic?

prateek: please do. i'll instrument cuda memcpy offsets + alignment checks and try to repro locally with a tiny C shim that simulates packed int4 arrays. cc @alon.

irene: thanks team. ping when PRs land and i'll re-run a week-long stability burn. :thumbsup:
